scenarios: Every available non-Void Bukkit particle type is configured without a payload and emitted through actual native held-use input; native payload bytes and a successful action outcome are observed.

Explicit dust RGB/scale, transition colors, ARGB entity-effect opacity, spell color/power, block states, custom item metadata, signed scalar rotation, integer shriek delay, trail color/duration, block/entity vibration destinations and available geyser water/impulse values are encoded in native particle packets.
Cloud count/spread/speed/offset/force, half-block line samples and zero-count signed directional emission are observed on the connected native client.
Actual native entity use supplies a living victim to trail and following-vibration destinations. A block-use plan with no victim produces no sample and reports failure through action flow.

Pre-cancelled native use emits no particle and runs no success action. A separate public projectile-event case anchors the emitter in one resident far chunk and confirms the offset destination remains unloaded and emits no successful action.

Thirty-one invalid particle shapes, types, ranges, unknown fields and excessive budgets reject the candidate before publication; each preserves an existing live item, and the restored candidate validates.
The exact candidate repeats the 118-check projectile suite on Spigot/Paper 1.21.11/26.3 and 45 core/bundle checks on all nine builds.
development_findings: Paper 26.3 exposes public Particle.Geyser payload objects where Spigot exposes integers. Configuration-time public constructors adapt that API difference without linking newer classes into the baseline or using server implementation reflection.

The original action inventory identifies typed-data particle helpers but does not establish BlocksAdder payload fields. The schema and code are independently designed; original implementation/assets/configurations were not copied or executed.
fixture_corrections: Spell particle colors encode ARGB, unlike RGB dust. The private expected spell bytes were corrected from a zero alpha to the actual opaque API color.

A nearby offset chunk was already resident in the native player view, so absence of a distant client packet did not prove an unloaded emitter. The final separate API scenario uses a controlled distant resident anchor and checks its unloaded offset chunk before and after execution.

The 26.3 native particle codec adds three speed axes, a VarInt count and randomization type after payload/flags/coordinates. Official server codec inspection informed the private bounded observer; the old fixed-tail assumption was corrected without changing production emission.
method: Java 21 clean Maven package and class-file major 65; actual Java 21 servers for 1.21.11 and Java 25 servers for 26.x. No production ProtocolLib dependency is required by these actions.

Native protocol 774 and 775 use installed public client codecs. Protocols 776/777 use the retained private loopback codec and official registry/packet evidence. Only the particle packet forms/counts exercised here are decoded; this is not a complete Minecraft client.

Final accepted runs use the same frozen plugin and particle-probe artifacts. Earlier implementation/observer/fixture failures are excluded from totals. Native input/packet, public API and headless metadata checks remain distinct scopes.

No fresh REA runtime evidence is claimed. Retained archive evidence and public API/dependency inspections informed requirements. No graphical Minecraft client, launcher or screenshot automation was used.
limitations: Totals include repeated native/API/data and headless assertions, not that many distinct player interactions or complete original-feature parity.

The new particle suite and core/bundle suite cover nine builds; projectile regressions cover four endpoints. Other historical suites were not rerun for this artifact and retain their separate artifact evidence.
No global particle rate limiter, future unknown data class, typed play_effect payload, script/gun provider or wider tracked feature family is established by these checks.
Minecraft rendering, alpha interpretation and perceived appearance remain user verification. Force/distance semantics remain native server behavior.

Temporary tools/servers remain ignored locally after earlier automatic approval review rejected cleanup. No test source, original artifact/asset or foreign configuration is in Git or the distributed JAR.
